start.researchCursor: disposable service adapter -> stateful API generation -> richer network fault injection -> isolation/replay/trace

improvement.title: Zero-dependency disposable real-service acceptance
improvement.materialGain: Ferrum now has a repeatable real local-versus-container service acceptance workload using its native process/http-request evidence contracts, with explicit container runtime/image identity and cleanup proof, without adding a permanent Node dependency.

continuityFix.problem: The repository's durable STATUS.json still pointed at an older product even though run 22 had a newer verified product checkpoint.
continuityFix.proof: The existing monotonic STATUS test failed on the first broad proposal run and identified verifiedWorkflowRun 32134811799 as newer than the stale STATUS value.
continuityFix.resolution: Advanced STATUS to the already-verified run-22 product and artifacts without weakening the monotonic test.

candidateExperiment.reason: Two real runs proved the lifecycle/identity/cleanup model but also proved the permanent client dependency and setup were unnecessary for Ferrum's current single-service acceptance lane.

comparison.additionalSetupRemoved: 12-15 seconds of Testcontainers installation and 198 added packages per clean CI job
comparison.parity: Same Ferrum POST/GET assertions, full response artifacts, runtime/image identity, and explicit cleanup proof retained.

maximumImprovementChallenge.question: Does Ferrum need Testcontainers as a permanent dependency to gain the disposable-service capability?
maximumImprovementChallenge.result: No for the current acceptance workload.
maximumImprovementChallenge.action: Kept the proven lifecycle/identity/cleanup ideas, replaced the client library with the Docker CLI already present on the Linux CI host, and re-ran the full exact-head acceptance surface.
maximumImprovementChallenge.antiChurn: No general container adapter, multi-container framework, or additional service abstraction was added without a demonstrated need.

ecosystemRotation: disposable services, stateful API generation, service virtualization, network/chaos faults, API fuzzing and load

candidates.purpose: Disposable containerized test dependencies and lifecycle management.
candidates.architecture: Node client over container runtimes with GenericContainer, mapped ports, wait strategies and explicit teardown.
candidates.harvest: Random mapped ports, bounded readiness, runtime/image identity and explicit removal proof.
candidates.integrationMode: Architecture transplant into Ferrum-native Docker fixture; retain as benchmark/reference.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Repeatable clean services without persistent host state.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Docker-compatible runtime plus large Node client dependency if used directly.
candidates.platformCoverage: Linux/macOS/Windows where supported container runtimes exist.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Runtime differences, image pulls, daemon availability, dependency/install overhead.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No blocker found for experiment; direct client was unnecessary overhead for current one-container case.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Two exact Ferrum experiment workflows passed with full evidence and cleanup proof.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Completed: identical local and container stateful HTTP fixture.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Same HTTP/evidence result, explicit identity/cleanup, bounded setup, full Ferrum gates.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Ferrum needs multi-container orchestration, portable Podman/containerd support, or reusable service dependency graphs.

candidates.maintenanceFreshness: very active; head checked same day
candidates.purpose: Property-based and stateful testing from OpenAPI/GraphQL schemas.
candidates.architecture: Schema-driven examples, coverage, fuzzing and stateful phases backed by Hypothesis-style generation/shrinking.
candidates.harvest: Fixed-seed bounded stateful sequences, operation dependency discovery, shrinking/minimization and failure classification.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Find API state defects that fixed handwritten flows miss while producing smaller repeatable reproducers.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Python runtime and Schemathesis package for isolated experiment.
candidates.platformCoverage: Cross-platform Python plus reachable HTTP service.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Generated workload volume, non-determinism without seed control, schema quality dependency.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No material blocker found in current scout.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Mature schema-driven API testing project with active 2026 development.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Run a fixed-seed bounded stateful workload against a disposable intentionally-defective OpenAPI fixture.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Find planted state defect, shrink to repeatable seed/sequence, retain Ferrum service/evidence identity, bounded elapsed time.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Next API-testing rotation or a Ferrum project with an OpenAPI service.

candidates.purpose: Deterministic network fault injection through TCP proxies.
candidates.architecture: Proxy server controlled through HTTP API with composable toxics such as latency, timeout/reset and bandwidth constraints.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Service/API recovery testing beyond binary browser offline mode.
candidates.harvest: Exact fault configuration as evidence plus deterministic inject/remove/recovery sequences.
candidates.integrationMode: Disposable sidecar fixture controlled by Ferrum process/http actions.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Repeatable latency/reset/timeout recovery proof for arbitrary services.
candidates.platformCoverage: Cross-platform deployment, easiest in Linux container CI.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: TCP-level semantics differ from browser offline emulation; latency toxic directionality issue #655 requires care.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Latency toxic directionality behavior tracked in upstream issue #655.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Widely used production testing proxy with explicit toxic API.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Place the new disposable service behind Toxiproxy and inject latency then reset with exact configuration evidence.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Fault observed deterministically, recovery succeeds after removal, no evidence loss, bounded overhead.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: After Schemathesis experiment or when service recovery behavior is under test.

candidates.purpose: Chaos testing for containers and networks.

nextExperiments: Run fixed-seed bounded Schemathesis stateful API generation against a disposable intentionally-defective OpenAPI fixture and require a minimized repeatable reproducer.
Put the same disposable service behind Toxiproxy and prove deterministic latency/reset/recovery with exact fault configuration evidence.
Compare WuppieFuzz and EvoMaster against the same planted API defect only after the lower-cost Schemathesis baseline exists.
Then rotate back to nsjail isolation parity, rr deterministic replay, Perfetto correlation and bounded strace failure diagnostics.
guardrails: No existing Ferrum target, browser, workload, evidence, fidelity, quantity, or runtime gate was removed or reduced.
The service fixture is additive and Linux-hosted because its purpose is disposable Docker parity; Windows Ferrum coverage remains fully exercised by the unchanged broad CI.
External fuzz/chaos tools remain isolated experiments until identical-workload evidence proves material capability or reliability gains.
Testcontainers is not rejected globally; it is superseded only for the current one-container acceptance lane by a proven lower-overhead path.
